column3: VB.NET console app that references two C# class libraries (.NET and .NET Standard 2.0) added to the same solution; builds and runs the solution in Visual Studio and validates console output.

column4: Trigger
Read the current user's home directory (for later cleanup).
Open Visual Studio.
Launch devenv and wait for its main window.
Maximize the Visual Studio window.

column3: Create Visual Basic console app project
column4: Click create new project.
Make sure language filter is set to Visual Basic.
Locate the template search box.
Click the template search box.
Search for console app.
Locate the Console App (Visual Basic) template result.
Select the Console App template.
Click Next to proceed past the template gallery.
Read the default project name so later steps can locate it by its real name.
Accept the default project name/location and continue to framework selection.
Notice the selected framework version and ensure the latest available version is selected.
Create project.
Wait for the solution to finish loading into the IDE (window is re-created at this stage).
Make sure Solution Explorer is opened.
Close the Live Unit Testing pane if Visual Studio auto-opened it.
Locate Program.vb under the VB console app project in Solution Explorer.
Open Program.vb in the editor to give it focus.
Select all existing code in Program.vb.
Copy the replacement Visual Basic code to the clipboard.
Replace the code with the console app implementation.
Save Program.vb.
Locate the Solution node in Solution Explorer.
Left click on the Solution node in solution explorer to ensure it has focus.
Right click on the Solution node in solution explorer.
Locate the resulting context menu popup window.
Click Add.
Click New Project.
Make sure language filter is set to C#.
Locate the template search box.
Click the template search box.
Search for Class Library.
Locate the Class Library (C#) template result.
Select the Class Library template.
Click Next to proceed past the template gallery.
Read the default project name so later steps can locate it by its real name.
Accept the default project name/location and continue to framework selection.
Notice the selected framework version and ensure .NET is selected.
Create project.
Locate Class1.cs under ClassLibrary1 in Solution Explorer.
Open Class1.cs in the editor.
Delete all code in Library.fs.
Copy the ClassLibrary1 implementation to the clipboard.
Replace the code with the ClassLibrary1 implementation.
Save Class1.cs.
Locate the Solution node in Solution Explorer.
Left click on the Solution node in solution explorer to ensure it has focus.
Right click on the Solution node in solution explorer.
Locate the resulting context menu popup window.
Click Add.
Click New Project.
Make sure language filter is set to C#.
Locate the template search box.
Click the template search box.
Search for Class Library.
Locate the Class Library (C#) template result.
Select the Class Library template.
Click Next to proceed past the template gallery.
Read the default project name so later steps can locate it by its real name.
Accept the default project name/location and continue to framework selection.
Notice the selected framework version and select .NET Standard 2.0.
Create project.
Locate Class1.cs under ClassLibrary2 in Solution Explorer.
Open Class1.cs in the editor.
Delete all code in Library.fs.
Copy the ClassLibrary2 implementation to the clipboard.
Replace the code with the ClassLibrary2 implementation.
Save Class1.cs.
Locate the VB console app project node in solution explorer.
Left click on the VB console app project node in solution explorer to ensure it has focus.
Right click on the VB console app project node in solution explorer.
Locate the resulting context menu popup window.
Click Add.
Click Project Reference.
Locate the Reference Manager dialog window.
Find the ClassLibrary1 reference row and checkbox edge.
Activate Reference Manager before checking ClassLibrary1.
Check ClassLibrary1 through the visible Reference Manager checkbox.
Find the ClassLibrary2 reference row and checkbox edge.
Activate Reference Manager before checking ClassLibrary2.
Select the ClassLibrary2 row before checking its checkbox.
Check ClassLibrary2 through the visible Reference Manager checkbox.
Find OK in Reference Manager.
Activate Reference Manager before committing the project reference.
Add the project references.
Build the solution.
Validate result is success.
Take screenshot.
Re-focus Program.vb in the editor before running.
Run the app without debugging.
Locate the running console window.
Validate result, take screenshot.
Take screenshot.
column16: Console shows Hello World!, Hi E2E and Hi All 8/9/2026.

column4: Close the console window.
Close the Visual Studio window.
Launch a titled command prompt (conhost) in the home dir to remove the scaffolded solution folder.
Focus the command prompt window.
Type the cleanup command to remove the scaffolded solution folder (VB console app + both class libraries).
Run the cleanup command.
Close the command prompt window.
column16: Command prompt closed; all scaffolded files cleaned up.
